scope: Independent design review only; no implementation or provider calls
strongest_objection: Resolved at design level. The strongest remaining implementation risk is preserving the documented journal-first Session/seed publication boundary on every success, failure and blocked scheduler path.

rounds.strongest_objection: The journal does not define the current action's publication/commit boundary. Stopping before another action still permits the latest accepted state/selection to be absent from replay, and appendFileResult can leave a partial final NDJSON record.

blocking_issues.problem: Journal append failure and interruption recovery are underspecified relative to host state and seed advancement.
blocking_issues.fix: Stage the pure host output and selection, durably persist the complete corresponding input/output/metadata before publishing the new Session, selected dialogue or advanced seed. Define complete-record framing and recovery for a partially written final record, or use an atomic bounded journal replacement. Failure must keep the prior session/request/seed authoritative and stop further actions.
tests: Inject persistence failure after a valid host operation is staged; prior authoritative state and seed remain unchanged and no success/dialogue is published.
Simulate a partial final journal write; earlier committed records remain replayable and the incomplete action is visibly uncommitted.
Replay every successfully published action from journal without cache, AI or policy files.

rounds.resolution: The corrected design stages pure host output and proposed seed, publishes a complete bounded whole-file journal through same-directory temporary write and atomic rename, then accepts/displays new Session and seed. Failed or partial temporary writes preserve prior journal and authoritative state. Blocked outputs are explicitly included, and no fsync or silent tail-repair claim is made.
additional_corrections: Explicit seed, signature, bundle, variant, text, weight, coefficient, context and token limits.
Cache lookup rechecked under per-key lock and first-use policy creation rechecked under its exclusive lock.
Original generation usage retained separately from zero new calls/tokens on a cache hit.
required_implementation_evidence: Failure injection for staged successful and blocked actions, temporary-write failure and rename failure; previous Session/seed/journal stay authoritative and success is not shown.
Complete journal replay without cache, AI or editable policy files.
Compile probe for actual supported effect-budget syntax; no claim of an enforced annotation without evidence.

implementation_controls: Recheck cache existence and signature after acquiring the per-key lock; never overwrite a valid bundle created by another run between initial lookup and lock acquisition.
Protect first-use policy initialization with exclusive ownership and recheck inside it; an existing editable policy must never be silently overwritten.
Separate original bundle-generation token metadata from this resolution's usage. A cache hit spends zero new provider calls/tokens while retaining the original generation provenance.
Specify numeric policy/seed/text bounds and checked arithmetic in the native controls. A growing persistent library has no stated total-storage cap; avoid claiming globally bounded storage.
Verify supported effect-budget syntax against the selected runtime; pinned v0.52.0 rejected the earlier literal @limit attribute. Do not claim an enforced annotation without a compiling probe.
supported_findings: Existing Request.context provides actor-local perception and existing host retains consent/authority/revision mechanics.
Author-provided OCEAN/value/fatigue/trust weights and one-hot confidence1 are explicitly experimental policy, with no calibrated model probability claim.
Exact signature matching and included stored signature give a conservative context boundary; retained identity makes missed reuse explicit.
Core std/fs exposes Result-returning mkdir/rename/read/write/append functions, std/ai.step exposes typed Result plus token usage, std/crypto.sha256Hex is pure.
Bounded attempted calls, visible errors and explicit authored continuation preserve provider failure legibility; account/model availability appropriately remains pending live smoke.
